Definition: from G3727; to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin:--adjure, charge.
BiblicalUsage: horkízō means adjure, charge. It turns up twice, in Mark and Acts.
TheologicalSignificance: I take horkízō as it stands — adjure, charge — and read the passage with that plain sense in mind.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Heals the Gerasene Demoniac; The Sons of Sceva at Ephesus
